memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then they got Joseph's robe, slaughtered a goat and dipped the robe in the blood. They took the ornate robe back to their father and said, 'We found this. Examine it to see whether it is your son's robe.' He recognized it and said, 'It is my son's robe! Some ferocious animal has devoured him. Joseph has surely been torn to pieces.'" - Gen 37:31-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
To cover their crime, the brothers take Joseph's robe, dip it in the blood of a slaughtered goat, and send it to their father with a cold, calculated question: "Examine it to see whether it is your son's robe." They let Jacob draw the devastating conclusion himself. And he does: "Some ferocious animal has devoured him."

There is a haunting irony in this scene. Years before, Jacob had deceived his own blind father using a garment and the skin of a goat, pretending to be his brother to steal a blessing (Gen 27:15-16). Now Jacob is deceived by his own sons using a garment and the blood of a goat. The deceiver has been deceived, in almost the same way he once deceived. "A man reaps what he sows" (Gal 6:7).

The brothers also show how sin multiplies. Having done evil to Joseph, they now pile on lies and cruelty toward their grieving father to cover their tracks. Sin rarely stays contained; it spreads, dragging in more deceit and wounding more people.

Two truths press on us. First, the seeds we sow have a way of returning to us; let us sow honesty and kindness rather than deceit. Second, when we do wrong, the way forward is confession, not cover-up. "Whoever conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy" (Prov 28:13).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I sowing seeds — honest or deceitful — that will return to me?
2. When I do wrong, do I confess it or cover it up?
3. Where do I need honesty instead of concealment?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to sow honesty and kindness, not deceit. When I do wrong, give me courage to confess rather than cover up, trusting Your mercy to those who come clean. Amen.
